documents.shelfmark: London, Wellcome Collection, MS.309 (b19695561), Johann Gerlach, Occulta scripta chymica (1572-76), section 'Secreta alchemica', handwritten pp.7-10 and 13-19 (scans 0012-0022) and parts of pp.40 (0043), 107 (0100), 112 (0105), 115 (0108), 156 (0149), 177 (0182)

plaintext.source: The manuscript carries a key by Julius Kohn (1889) on pp.260-261 (scans 0265-0266): rows of sign groups with no letters written beside them. No decipherment of the text is known here; the contributor found no earlier published reading (searches 10-11 Nov 2026).

transcription.source: Wellcome IIIF images (iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b19695561, Public Domain Mark), full resolution
transcription.notes: 6,479 lettered signs (not counting word dividers, = signs and damage marks) in 348 lines of 17 pages or parts of pages, counted at integration by an own parser of transcription.txt (not by docs/_check_profile.py --measure, so measured is false); 143 signs carried a doubt mark at integration, 96 after the re-reading of p.7 on the image (14 Nov 2026). Pages 7-10, 13-15, 19 and the partial pages by Claude (Anthropic); pp.16-18 first passes by GPT-6 Astra/Sol and Gemini 4 Argon (p.18 by two, adjudicated); pp.8, 9, 10 and 13 also read independently by GPT-6 Astra/Sol (agreement 91.6% to 99.6% sign by sign, contributor's figures; agreement is not accuracy). Compared with the image at integration: the first six lines of p.8 (130 signs), group by group: agree; the other pages were not compared. The inserted narrow leaf (pp.11-12) has no scan of its own; p.9 lines 21-25 and two lines of p.10 are damaged.

system.summary: A simple homophonic substitution of German with one to three (once four) pictorial signs per letter and a comma-like word divider; alchemical pictograms (antimony, Mars, Mercury, Sol) stand for themselves; no nulls, no code groups, no separate u/v or i/j.
system.notes: 52 sign labels in the contributor's table (key.tsv; the Wellcome catalogue says 51 symbols, not reconciled). Kohn's sheet runs from Z to A in groups of signs, with no letters written; the contributor set the values by that order and re-aligned three groups (u, t, s are one step out of line with the text values, he says). Three different figure-4 shapes (open, closed with a point, closed modern) stand for l, r and u and are partly assigned from context, mostly on p.7.

prior_solution.where: A key by Julius Kohn (1889) is written into the volume (pp.260-261), so the cipher was known to be solvable and its key was recorded; the Wellcome catalogue says 'Kohn's key inserted'. No published reading found by the contributor (10-11 Nov 2026); German specialist literature, Kohn's papers and the Wellcome files not checked.

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney directed the work and sent the result as GitHub issue #439; Claude and, for three pages, other model sessions transcribed from the images, applied the key, decoded and read. No reading by a person without AI.
tools: list of 64,029 spellings from 116 Deutsches Textarchiv texts of 1500-1599 for a real-word test, with 1,000 shuffled keys per page (contributor's; not sent)
models: GPT-6 Astra and Sol (OpenAI), Gemini 4 Argon (Google), Grok 4.7 (xAI): passes and review, as named by the contributor
Claude Opus (Anthropic): blind readers, judges, second reader, reading and English for pp.20-178 (28 Nov 2026)

solution.what: Catalogue entry 1252 (UK libraries sweep, 28-29 Oct 2026): Wellcome MS.309, 178 pages in a cipher, Kohn's key inserted at pp.260-261; not viewed then.

Kohn's key (1889, pp.260-261, scans 0265-0266) set up as a table of 52 sign labels with a letter each (key_v3): signs only on the sheet, so values by the order of the groups; the u, t, s groups moved one step against Kohn's order to fit the text; three figure-4 shapes told apart by context.
Sign-by-sign transcription of pp.7-10, 13-19 and parts of six later pages from the Wellcome IIIF scans: 348 lines, 6,479 lettered signs, 143 doubtful.

Real-word test: decoded words (2+ letters, no unknown sign) looked up in 64,029 sixteenth-century spellings: 77% (p.40) to 96% (p.112) per page; 1,000 shuffled keys per page reach at most 30% (p.112) and 26% (p.40). Contributor's figures; the word list and scorer were not sent.

Blind control on p.8: transcribed and decoded once with the key frozen, by the contributor's record: 529 signs, signs in words giving sense 489 firm (92.4%), 522 with probable readings (98.7%). Independent transcribers agree on 91.6% to 99.6% of signs.

The decode built into Early New High German sentences and translated for each page: recipes for flowers of sulphur (pp.7-10), flowers of antimony (pp.13-15), the 'corruption of Sol' with sal ammoniac, spiritus vini and aqua regis (pp.16-19), and the openings of later sections. Contributor's counts per page: firm 80.5% to 96.1% of signs on the five rated pages; pp.14-18 and the partial pages not rated.

Integration after an independent check from the issue text: own decoder written from the key table reproduces all 348 decoded lines from the sign transcription (0 differences, 6,479 signs); Kohn's two key leaves and the first six lines of p.8 compared with the Wellcome IIIF images; word-level count by the README rule from reading.md: 1,259 of 1,395 words read without a doubt mark or bracket = 90.3%. Not re-run: the word-list test and shuffles (list not sent).

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) from key.tsv and transcription.txt only: 348/348 lines give the letters of decryption.txt. p.7 re-read on the Wellcome IIIF image (b19695561_0012, full resolution, line bands): the open 4 (l), the closed 4 with the stem through ending in a point (r) and the flat-foot modern 4 (u) are distinct on the page; the 45 doubtful 4-shapes of p.7 all agree with their shapes and lose their '?'. Three corrections: L07 'PI LEO OL? PHI DOT 4R?' -> 'PI LEO PHI DOT 4L' (souil; no o+ sign, the curl belongs to LEO), L07 'SQ? LEO 4L? ST LAM' -> 'RH LEO 4L ST LAM' (wolet), L13 'EUR 4U? PLUS? ST TRI' -> 'EUR 4U 4R? ST TRI' (ruret: a pale figure 4, not a plain cross). p.7 doubtful signs 54 -> 7. transcription.txt and decryption.txt updated; reading.md left to the maintainer (suggested: souil ir wolet, ruret in wol umb).

Project check of PR #570 (Brice Dudout): his decoder re-run (348 of 348 lines). Lines L07, L08, L12 and L13 of p.7 (about 75 signs) compared with the full-size Wellcome image b19695561_0012: all agree with his corrected transcription, including the three changed signs (souil, wolet, ruret with a faded 4R?). reading.md p.7 updated (wolet without doubt mark; ruret? for ruhet? [ruret?]); count 1,260 of 1,394 words, 90.4% (was 1,259 of 1,395, 90.3%); doubtful signs 143 -> 96. Other pages not re-read.

pp.124-137 identified as the target of the margin references on p.19 (1. sal armoniack fol. 124, 2. spiritus vini fol. 125, 3. aqua regis fol. 137); 14 Wellcome IIIF images (scans 0117-0130) fetched by plain curl; all 14 pages are cipher, p.129 only about 3 lines.
Key frozen before any decode: upstream key.tsv (commit 89e25ef7d) copied byte for byte as key_frozen.tsv, sha256 7e6f0b8a...a9b3 (FREEZE.txt, 01:35:40Z). No change to the key before or after.

Blind sign transcription by two Claude sessions from a label sheet without letter values, told not to decipher: pp.124-130 (BLIND_a.tsv, frozen 01:49:00Z) and pp.131-137 (BLIND_b.tsv, frozen 01:46:04Z), merged as BLIND_all.tsv (sha256 33ed44b7...). 306 lines, 6,072 signs in the key, 143 doubt-marked.

One mechanical decode (decode_once.py, refuses a second run) of BLIND_all.tsv with the frozen key; then one strict judging pass of the decode, no emendation: S 5,667, E 398, N 32 of 6,097 letters = 92.9% (per page 90.8% to 94.8%; judge/JUDGE_NOTES.txt). The E letters are mostly four systematic slips: l for u/v 195, r for u 72, g for d/k 57, f for long s 27 (351 of 398), suspected key-table errors in key.tsv; not fixed (with them fixed the share would be about 98.7%, untested).

Shuffled-key control (blind/p124-137/shuffle.py): the letter column of key.tsv permuted among the sign labels, 5,000 shuffles at each of seeds 20261112 and 7, scored with lang model de-1500s (order 5, letters only) as mean log-prob per letter. Real decode -3.0196; shuffles >= real: 0 of 5,000 at both seeds (max -6.0697 and -5.9688). Pass (rule: fewer than 5).

docs/_check_reading.py on the pp.124-137 files: reading_p124-137.md clean share 0.239 (43/180 sentences, holes 0.203), decryption_p124-137.txt 0.241: 'not a reading' (below 0.60). The judge's [x] slip marks split words into fragments the word list does not know, and the line-end run-ons are left as written; the text entry is recorded as 'decoded, not read', by the checker's state.

texts.label: Gerlach, Occulta scripta chymica, pp.7-10, 13-19 and parts of pp.40, 107, 112, 115, 156, 177
texts.summary: Alchemical and medical recipes of a 1570s German notebook: how to make flowers of sulphur and to prepare sublimed sulphur three times with colcothar and salt as a medicine for the lungs and chest (pp.7-10), flowers of antimony red and white, with a fever remedy (pp.13-15), how to make quicksilver out of gold, and the numbered preparations 'belonging to the corruption of Sol': sal ammoniac sublimed through rock salt, spiritus vini from burnt wine and tartar, and aqua regis (pp.16-19); the openings of later sections on the philosopher's stone, putrefaction, the mercury of Sol and Luna and the arcanum of tartar are read in part.

reading_review.by: integration reader for the project (a model session, not a person), 12 Nov 2026
reading_review.note: Read as Early New High German sentences against decryption.txt and translation.md on pp.7, 8, 13 and 19: coherent recipe prose with the technical vocabulary of the time (schwewel, colcothar, uitriol, sublimir, helm, viola, weinstein). p.9 and p.10 hold stained or damaged lines with real holes. The pages are the contributor's reading of a 52-label table he aligned himself to Kohn's sheet; the decode is reproduced from his own transcription, which was compared with the image on six lines of p.8 only.

texts.label: Gerlach, Occulta scripta chymica, pp.124-137 (sal armoniack, spiritus vini with tartar, the balneum roris, aqua regis) - decoded, not read by the reading check
texts.summary: The sections that the margin of p.19 sends the reader to: the close of a mercury preparation; the sal armoniack sublimed with sal gemme (p.124); spirit of wine distilled from strong wine and separated from the brandy-wine (pp.125-127); the spirit sharpened with calcined tartar and put to putrefaction in a sealed viola inside an oak cask over a water kettle, with the furnace and the apparatus described (pp.127-135), the process called balneum roris (p.136); and the aqua regis, defined against aqua fortis, from saltpetre and calcined Hungarian vitriol (p.137). English is a recipe-level summary by an AI model, unchecked.
